title: 1959 AHSME Problem 32
statement: The length \(l\) of a tangent, drawn from a point \(A\) to a circle, is \(\dfrac43\) of the radius \(r.\) The (shortest) distance from \(A\) to the circle is:

solutions.text:
If \(O\) is the center and \(T\) the point of tangency, then \(OT\perp AT.\) Hence \[ \begin{aligned} AO &=\sqrt{r^2+l^2}\\ &=\sqrt{r^2+\frac{16r^2}{9}}\\ &=\frac{5r}{3}. \end{aligned} \] The shortest distance from \(A\) to the circle is \(AO-r=\frac{2r}{3}.\) Since \(l=\frac{4r}{3},\) this distance equals \(\frac{l}{2}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Join \(A\) to the center and to the point of tangency
Use the right triangle with legs \(r\) and \(l=\frac{4r}{3}\)
